scheme_name: e-Challan Amnesty Scheme: 50% concession on pending traffic fines (Nov 2026–Jan 2027)
note: Kerala's Motor Vehicles Department opened a new e-Challan Amnesty Scheme on 1 November 2026, running until 31 January 2027: a 50% concession on fines for eligible MV Act/Rules challans issued by the MVD or Kerala Police up to 31 March 2026, where no court proceedings have started; later challans get no discount. It follows an e-Challan Amnesty Scheme announced in the state's revised 2026-27 Budget (presented 19 June 2026), but no G.O. or circular number for the scheme itself was found online as of this check. Confirmed instead against the MVD's own live application portal (services.mvd.kerala.gov.in/etax/otc), which today runs a 'One Time Challan Settlement Under Amnesty Scheme' application flow stating eligible challans are those 'generated up to March 31, 2026' with 'Payment deadline: January 31, 2027' — matching the press reports — and corroborated by two independent press reports (Onmanorama, 8 Oct 2026; The South First). Since the underlying order text itself was not read, readers should confirm the exact amount due on the MVD portal before paying. Re-checked 2 November 2026: the MVD's live application portal (services.mvd.kerala.gov.in/etax/otc) still runs the One Time Challan Settlement Under Amnesty Scheme flow, still stating challans 'generated up to March 31, 2026' are covered with a 'Payment deadline: January 31, 2027'. Onmanorama (8 Oct 2026) and The South First both still resolve with unchanged facts — 50% concession, pre-31 March 2026 challans only, court-proceedings-already-started excluded, 1 Nov 2026 to 31 Jan 2027 window. No newer order or press coverage found. Facts unchanged. Re-checked 4 November 2026: the MVD's live application portal (services.mvd.kerala.gov.in/etax/otc/application-closed) still runs the One Time Challan Settlement Under Amnesty Scheme flow, still showing challans 'generated up to March 31, 2026' as eligible with a 'Payment deadline: January 31, 2027', and the application form itself (not an application-closed notice) still active. Onmanorama (8 Oct 2026) and The South First both still resolve with the same 50% concession, pre-31 March 2026 eligibility, court-proceedings-excluded, and 1 Nov 2026-31 Jan 2027 window. A fresh web search found no official G.O./circular published for the scheme and no newer press coverage beyond these two reports. Facts unchanged. Re-checked 6 November 2026: the MVD's live application portal (services.mvd.kerala.gov.in/etax/otc/application-closed) still runs the One Time Challan Settlement Under Amnesty Scheme flow, still showing challans 'generated up to March 31, 2026' as eligible with a 'Payment deadline: January 31, 2027'. Onmanorama (8 Oct 2026) and The South First both still resolve with the same 50% concession, pre-31 March 2026 eligibility, court-proceedings-excluded, and 1 Nov 2026-31 Jan 2027 window. A fresh web search found no official G.O./circular published for the scheme and no newer press coverage beyond these two reports. Facts unchanged.

history.summary: Kerala's prior one-time amnesty was a 50% concession on pending motor vehicle fines, covering violations registered up to 31 December 2024 (cases already before the courts were excluded) with a payment deadline of 30 April 2026, against a backlog of 1,02,53,151 pending violations worth ₹932.64 crore. The Transport Department order behind it was never published online, so the record relied on press sources and the MVD's own application portal. Reconfirmed 1 November 2026: the MVD portal now serves the new Nov 2026–Jan 2027 scheme in its place, and both press sources still resolve with unchanged facts.
